findings.description: Frozen max_diff_lines=1500 is exceeded: baseline-to-candidate numstat sums to 1866 added lines across 9 allowed files (0 deleted). Protected inputs unchanged and file-count budget passes, but scope budget does not. Stop this frozen run; any additional remediation requires a separately scoped contract, not a second primary repair or expanded takeover.

select readiness is followed by blocking BufferedReader.read(min(4096,budget)). Child writes one byte then sleeps .6 seconds with timeout .1: returned completed at .616 seconds; both streams short+sleep also completed at .617 seconds. Long-lived short output can hang indefinitely and bypass cancellation. Drain uses unbounded read after leader exit, risking budget memory and inherited-pipe hangs.

Injected killpg PermissionError caused timeout result tree_cleanup_confirmed=true while an independently checked descendant remained alive. Fallback kills only leader and wait confirms only leader. Injected drive exception also leaves leader alive: outer process variable is never assigned and finally only closes pipes. Reviewer terminated all probe children afterward.

Valid completed protocol with ProcessResult(status=timed_out,exit_code=0,truncated=false) is parsed as completed. Actual process status must gate success and noncompleted statuses map unchanged regardless of exit0.

Valid model=test-model, summary=retain summary and artifact result.txt are silently replaced by model null, empty summary and empty artifacts. Parser accepts artifacts=null, boolean token counts and schema_version=true; boolean usage output violates schema integer types. Complete strict validation and preserve valid fields.

Child exits successfully after exactly 64 output bytes with budget64; runner reports output_limit/truncated=true. Reaching exact budget does not prove excess: EOF streams in readiness list spuriously trigger limit. Draining truncation also does not propagate a truncation flag.

Windows ordinary short processes with require_tree_cleanup=false remain unsupported: select.select only supports sockets on Windows, but implementation passes subprocess pipes and suppresses OSError into empty readiness, eventually timing out. Linux simulation of pipe-select OSError reproduces timed_out; actual Windows runtime unrun. POSIX still uses thread-unsafe preexec_fn=os.setpgrp.
